quote: Yeah. I can see that's probably where those 200 bills are at here. July and August is pretty high.
stewart_read: Rep reflected the bill number back and connected it to seasonal usage, which is a form of curiosity creation, but never converted it into an explicit reason to act (no 'that's money you could be putting toward your own system instead of ComEd' framing). Capture-and-acknowledge occurred; the flip into alignment-against-the-utility did not.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged that with an easy, cooperative, already-warm customer, an aggressive flip risked feeling like a sales pitch he didn't need — but there's no direct evidence in the transcript that this was a deliberate choice rather than an omission.
coaching_implication: Coach the specific line: after reflecting the seasonal bill pattern, add one sentence that turns the number into a felt cost ('that's money going to ComEd every summer instead of building equity in your own system') before moving to scheduling.

quote: Now the only requirement for our program is that you have a credit score above 670. Is that the case?
stewart_read: Rep stated the correct 670 threshold (unlike the 650 drift seen in other calls) and moved on cleanly once the customer self-reported 800.
coaching_implication: No action needed — this is a clean example of the qualifier script run correctly and can be used as a positive reference clip.

quote: Alright. So go ahead. Take a photo of that. And then I sent you a text message where you can text that photo over to me.
stewart_read: Rep executed the mail/online branching correctly by pivoting to a text-photo capture live on the call, resulting in the bill document actually being received during the call rather than deferred.
coaching_implication: Positive reference: this live capture avoided the 8-15 minute bill-collection slog seen in other calls (SESSION6, SESSION14) by using the text-photo path efficiently.

quote: You cannot just send it to me through email or something?
stewart_read: This is a proposal-by-email ask, correctly identified and handled per the hard rule ('We we like to go through it with you'), but the rep did not use the objection-inversion move available here — e.g., reframing that going it alone without walkthrough is what actually costs him money/time versus the quick call.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep's canonical hard-rule response was sufficient and the customer dropped the ask immediately without further resistance, so a flip may have been unnecessary friction on an already-cooperative call.
coaching_implication: Minor — note as a missed opportunity to deploy the escape-hatch language with a persuasive frame, but not a call-losing gap since the customer complied right after.

quote: Either way, you're gonna send me a copy on everything. Right?
stewart_read: The rep agreed to email a copy after the appointment, but the button-up sequence that follows skips the 'is that fair?' handshake and the no-driving/computer instruction — the call closes on logistics (grabbing an email address) rather than a clean recap-and-confirm.
alternative_hypothesis: The core appointment details (day, time, phone number) were already locked earlier at 08:51-08:58, so the call may have been functionally closed before this exchange and the email question is just a tail-end administrative note rather than a structural failure.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to close with the full button-up recap (day, time, one-hour block, no-driving/computer instruction, 'is that fair?') even when the appointment was set earlier in the call — don't let a late administrative question replace the formal handshake.

quote: What's got you looking at solar for the home?
stewart_read: Rep asked the interest question early and got a generic answer ('just thinking about it, see how much I'm looking at'), then moved on without probing depth.
alternative_hypothesis: The customer's answer itself was thin and non-committal ('just trying to get estimates'), giving the rep little material to expand on — the schema flags depth as valuable but the customer didn't hand over an emotional anchor to work with, so probing further may have yielded nothing new.
coaching_implication: Low priority — the customer's answer was genuinely shallow, so this is more a customer-limitation than a rep skill gap; worth one follow-up question in future calls ('what would switching to solar mean for you?') but not a coaching priority here.

stewart_read: Customer voiced a scheduling-anxiety question mid-booking; rep answered directly and specifically ('We usually call within five minutes') which is the correct firm-time-anchor pattern.
coaching_implication: Positive — use as an example of confident, specific time-anchoring rather than a vague reassurance.
